transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, well, what finally scared me into coming in today is that I keep making these really dumb technical mistakes at work. I work as a camera operator and video editor, and I'm doing things I definitely know better than to make. 

Like... I'll label camera cards wrong, or I'll just completely miss a timecode note. Recently I even exported a client cut with the wrong lower-third on the screen, and the frustrating part is that happened even after I had already checked it. It's just really starting to worry me.
Have you had similar attention or careless-mistake problems since childhood?

Yeah, I have. Um... even back in elementary school, my teachers actually had to move my desk a lot. I was just always getting out of my seat, or blurting out answers in class. I would end up bothering my classmates before I even realized I was doing it. So, yeah, it's been happening for a long time.
Do you still feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still now as an adult?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um, a good example is when I have to sit through a client screening for a video. Sitting still through those... it honestly feels like there’s this pressure building up under my skin. I just feel like I need to get up and do something with my body, even when I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly.
